choice: Limited the attachment list to model types the user can view, and made single-attachment reads return 403 without view permission, because any logged-in user could read every attachment and its file URL.
final:
I fixed a read-access hole in the attachment API: any logged-in user could list or fetch any attachment, including its file URL, even without permission to view the object it's attached to. All 52 tests in the requested set pass.

**The problem:** creating, editing and deleting attachments all check the user's permission on the parent object (part, purchase order, sales order, build, etc.). Reading didn't check at all. Someone with no role on, say, purchase orders could call `GET /api/attachment/` and see every purchase order attachment, then download the files through `/media/`. That endpoint only checks that the user is logged in.

**The change** (`src/backend/InvenTree/common/api.py`):
- **List endpoint:** results are now limited to attachments whose parent type the user can view, using the same per-model check the write paths use. Superusers still see everything.
- **Detail endpoint:** opening a single attachment now returns 403 if the user can't view the parent type. I first applied the filter to the detail endpoint too, but that made edit and delete requests from users without view rights return 404. An existing test expects 403 there, so the detail endpoint uses an explicit check instead.
- Added an explicit `import common.validators`; it previously only worked because another import pulled it in.

**Not covered:**
- I didn't add a test for the new filtering. The existing tests confirm nothing broke, but nothing yet proves a user without view rights is actually blocked.
- `/media/` still serves any file to any logged-in user who knows its path. Paths are predictable (`attachments/<model>/<id>/<filename>`), so file contents are still reachable that way; this change only stops the API from handing out the links. Closing that fully needs a per-file check on media requests, which is a larger change.

Nothing is committed and no PR is open. Per the project rules, a human needs to review this before it's submitted.

CHOICE: Limited the attachment list to model types the user can view, and made single-attachment reads return 403 without view permission, because any logged-in user could read every attachment and its file URL.
